messages.content: What is Ring and how do I create a basic HTTP server?

Ring is Clojure's HTTP server abstraction. It's a specification for handlers, middleware, and request/response maps - similar to Python's WSGI or Ruby's Rack. **Core Concepts** - **Handler**: Function that takes a request map, returns a response map - **Middleware**: Function that wraps handlers to add functionality - **Request/Response**: Clojure maps with specific keys **Setup** ```clojure ;; deps.edn {:deps {ring/ring-core {:mvn/version "1.10.0"} ring/ring-jetty-adapter {:mvn/version "1.10.0"}}} ``` **Hello World** ```clojure (require '[ring.adapter.jetty :as jetty]) ;; Handler - a function that returns a response map (defn handler [request] {:status 200 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"} :body "Hello, World!"}) ;; Start server (jetty/run-jetty handler {:port 3000}) ;; Server runs on http://localhost:3000 ``` **Request Map** ```clojure ;; Ring request map structure {:server-port 3000 :server-name "localhost" :remote-addr "127.0.0.1" :uri "/users/123" :query-string "active=true" :scheme :http :request-method :get :protocol "HTTP/1.1" :headers {"host" "localhost:3000" "accept" "application/json" "user-agent" "curl/7.64.1"} :body #object[InputStream]} ;; Access request parts (defn handler [request] (let [method (:request-method request) ; :get, :post, :put, :delete uri (:uri request) ; "/users/123" params (:query-string request) ; "active=true" headers (:headers request)] ; {"host" "localhost"...} {:status 200 :body (str "Method: " method " URI: " uri)})) ``` **Response Map** ```clojure ;; Basic response {:status 200 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/html"} :body "

Hello

"} ;; JSON response {:status 200 :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"} :body "{\"message\": \"success\"}"} ;; Redirect {:status 302 :headers {"Location" "/dashboard"} :body ""} ;; Not Found {:status 404 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"} :body "Not Found"} ;; Error {:status 500 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"} :body "Internal Server Error"} ``` **Response Helpers** ```clojure (require '[ring.util.response :as response]) ;; Create responses easily (response/response "Hello") ; 200 with body (response/not-found "Page not found") ; 404 (response/bad-request "Invalid input"); 400 (response/redirect "/login") ; 302 redirect (response/created "/users/123") ; 201 with Location header ;; Add headers (-> (response/response "Hello") (response/content-type "text/plain") (response/header "X-Custom" "value")) ;; Status helpers (response/status (response/response "OK") 201) ``` **Routing (Manual)** ```clojure (defn handler [request] (let [{:keys [uri request-method]} request] (case [request-method uri] [:get "/"] {:status 200 :body "Home"} [:get "/about"] {:status 200 :body "About"} [:get "/users"] {:status 200 :body "List users"} [:post "/users"] {:status 201 :body "User created"} ;; Default - 404 {:status 404 :body "Not Found"}))) ``` **Using Compojure for Routing** ```clojure ;; deps.edn {:deps {compojure/compojure {:mvn/version "1.7.0"}}} (require '[compojure.core :refer [defroutes GET POST PUT DELETE]] '[compojure.route :as route]) (defroutes app (GET "/" [] "Home") (GET "/about" [] "About") (GET "/users" [] "List users") (GET "/users/:id" [id] (str "User " id)) (POST "/users" [] "Create user") (PUT "/users/:id" [id] (str "Update user " id)) (DELETE "/users/:id" [id] (str "Delete user " id)) (route/not-found "Not Found")) (jetty/run-jetty app {:port 3000}) ``` **Server Options** ```clojure ;; Development - auto-reload friendly (def server (jetty/run-jetty #'handler ; Use var for REPL reloading {:port 3000 :join? false})) ; Don't block thread ;; Stop server (.stop server) ;; Production (jetty/run-jetty handler {:port 3000 :host "0.0.0.0" ; Listen on all interfaces :join? true ; Block main thread :ssl? true :ssl-port 443 :keystore "keystore.jks" :key-password "secret"}) ```
How do I create and use Ring middleware?

Middleware in Ring are functions that wrap handlers to add cross-cutting functionality like logging, authentication, or parsing.

**Middleware Pattern**
```clojure
;; Middleware is a function that takes a handler and returns a new handler
(defn wrap-example [handler]
  (fn [request]
    ;; Before: modify request or do pre-processing
    (let [response (handler request)]  ; Call wrapped handler
      ;; After: modify response or do post-processing
      response)))

;; Apply middleware
(def app (wrap-example handler))
```

**Logging Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-logging [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [start (System/currentTimeMillis)
          {:keys [request-method uri]} request]
      (println "-->" (name request-method) uri)
      (let [response (handler request)
            elapsed (- (System/currentTimeMillis) start)]
        (println "<--" (:status response) (str elapsed "ms"))
        response))))

;; Usage
(def app (wrap-logging handler))
;; Logs:
;; --> GET /users
;; <-- 200 45ms
```

**Authentication Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-authentication [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [token (get-in request [:headers "authorization"])]
      (if-let [user (when token (verify-token token))]
        ;; Add user to request
        (handler (assoc request :user user))
        ;; Return 401
        {:status 401
         :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
         :body "{\"error\": \"Unauthorized\"}"}))))

;; Make some routes require auth
(defn wrap-require-auth [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (if (:user request)
      (handler request)
      {:status 401 :body "Authentication required"})))

;; Apply
(def public-handler 
  (-> handler
      wrap-authentication))  ; Adds :user if token valid

(def protected-handler
  (-> handler
      wrap-require-auth      ; Requires :user
      wrap-authentication))  ; Adds :user
```

**Error Handling Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-exceptions [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (try
      (handler request)
      (catch Exception e
        (println "Error:" (.getMessage e))
        {:status 500
         :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
         :body (str "{\"error\": \"" (.getMessage e) "\"}")}))
      (catch Throwable t
        (println "Critical error:" (.getMessage t))
        {:status 500
         :body "Internal Server Error"}))))

;; With custom exception types
(defn wrap-app-exceptions [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (try
      (handler request)
      (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e
        (let [{:keys [type status message]} (ex-data e)]
          (case type
            :validation {:status 400 :body message}
            :not-found {:status 404 :body message}
            :unauthorized {:status 401 :body message}
            {:status 500 :body "Server error"}))))))
```

**CORS Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-cors [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [response (if (= :options (:request-method request))
                     {:status 200 :body ""}
                     (handler request))]
      (-> response
          (assoc-in [:headers "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] "*")
          (assoc-in [:headers "Access-Control-Allow-Methods"] "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS")
          (assoc-in [:headers "Access-Control-Allow-Headers"] "Content-Type, Authorization")))))
```

**Request Parsing Middleware**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]])

;; Query params: "?name=alice&age=30"
;; wrap-params adds :query-params {"name" "alice" "age" "30"}
;; wrap-keyword-params converts to :params {:name "alice" :age "30"}

(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-params
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})  ; Parse JSON body
      wrap-json-response))                 ; Serialize response as JSON
```

**Content Negotiation**
```clojure
(defn wrap-content-type [handler content-type]
  (fn [request]
    (let [response (handler request)]
      (if (get-in response [:headers "Content-Type"])
        response
        (assoc-in response [:headers "Content-Type"] content-type)))))

;; Default to JSON
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-content-type "application/json")))
```

**Middleware with Configuration**
```clojure
(defn wrap-rate-limit [handler {:keys [max-requests window-ms]}]
  (let [requests (atom {})]  ; ip -> [timestamps]
    (fn [request]
      (let [ip (:remote-addr request)
            now (System/currentTimeMillis)
            cutoff (- now window-ms)
            recent (filter #(> % cutoff) (get @requests ip []))]
        (if (>= (count recent) max-requests)
          {:status 429 :body "Too Many Requests"}
          (do
            (swap! requests assoc ip (conj recent now))
            (handler request)))))))

;; Usage
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-rate-limit {:max-requests 100 :window-ms 60000})))
```

**Composing Middleware**
```clojure
;; Using ->
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-logging
      wrap-exceptions
      wrap-authentication
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-params
      wrap-json-body
      wrap-json-response
      wrap-cors))

;; Middleware applied inside-out:
;; Request  -> cors -> json-body -> params -> auth -> exceptions -> logging -> handler
;; Response <- cors <- json-resp <- params <- auth <- exceptions <- logging <- handler

;; Using comp (reverse order)
(def middleware
  (comp wrap-cors
        wrap-json-response
        wrap-json-body
        wrap-params
        wrap-keyword-params
        wrap-authentication
        wrap-exceptions
        wrap-logging))

(def app (middleware handler))
```

**Conditional Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-if [handler pred middleware]
  (if pred
    (middleware handler)
    handler))

;; Only apply in production
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-if (= :prod env) wrap-ssl-redirect)
      (wrap-if (= :dev env) wrap-reload)))

;; Route-specific middleware
(defn wrap-for-routes [handler routes middleware]
  (fn [request]
    (if (some #(re-matches % (:uri request)) routes)
      ((middleware handler) request)
      (handler request))))

(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-for-routes [#"/api/.*" #"/admin/.*"] wrap-authentication)))
```
How do I handle different content types and JSON in Ring?

Ring handles different content types through middleware for parsing requests and formatting responses.

**JSON Handling**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {ring/ring-json {:mvn/version "0.5.1"}
        ;; or use cheshire directly
        cheshire/cheshire {:mvn/version "5.12.0"}}}

(require '[ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]]
         '[cheshire.core :as json])
```

**Parsing JSON Requests**
```clojure
;; wrap-json-body parses JSON body into :body
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true   ; Convert keys to keywords
                       :bigdecimals? false})))

;; Handler receives parsed JSON
(defn create-user [request]
  (let [{:keys [name email]} (:body request)]  ; Already parsed!
    (println "Creating user:" name email)
    {:status 201
     :body {:id 1 :name name :email email}}))

;; Manual JSON parsing
(defn handler [request]
  (let [body (-> request :body slurp (json/parse-string true))]
    {:status 200
     :body body}))
```

**JSON Responses**
```clojure
;; wrap-json-response converts Clojure data to JSON
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-json-response  ; Automatically converts maps/vectors to JSON
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})))

(defn list-users [_]
  {:status 200
   :body [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}
          {:id 2 :name "Bob"}]})
;; Response body is automatically JSON: [{"id":1,"name":"Alice"},...]

;; Manual JSON response
(require '[cheshire.core :as json])

(defn list-users [_]
  {:status 200
   :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
   :body (json/generate-string [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}])})
```

**Form Data**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]])

;; For application/x-www-form-urlencoded
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-keyword-params  ; String keys -> keyword keys
      wrap-params))        ; Parse query string & form body

;; Handler
(defn login [request]
  (let [{:keys [username password]} (:params request)]
    (if (valid-credentials? username password)
      {:status 200 :body "Login successful"}
      {:status 401 :body "Invalid credentials"})))

;; POST /login with body: username=alice&password=secret
;; :params = {:username "alice" :password "secret"}
```

**Multipart File Upload**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.multipart-params :refer [wrap-multipart-params]])

(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-multipart-params))  ; Parse multipart/form-data

;; File upload handler
(defn upload-file [request]
  (let [{:keys [file]} (:params request)]
    ;; file is a map with :filename, :content-type, :tempfile, :size
    (println "Received:" (:filename file) (:size file) "bytes")
    
    ;; Copy temp file to permanent location
    (io/copy (:tempfile file) 
             (io/file "uploads" (:filename file)))
    
    {:status 200
     :body {:message "File uploaded"
            :filename (:filename file)}}))

;; curl -F "file=@photo.jpg" http://localhost:3000/upload
```

**Content Negotiation**
```clojure
;; Check Accept header for response format
(defn handler [request]
  (let [accept (get-in request [:headers "accept"] "application/json")
        data {:users [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}]}]
    (cond
      (clojure.string/includes? accept "application/json")
      {:status 200
       :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
       :body (json/generate-string data)}
      
      (clojure.string/includes? accept "application/edn")
      {:status 200
       :headers {"Content-Type" "application/edn"}
       :body (pr-str data)}
      
      (clojure.string/includes? accept "text/html")
      {:status 200
       :headers {"Content-Type" "text/html"}
       :body (render-html data)}
      
      :else
      {:status 406 :body "Not Acceptable"})))
```

**Using Muuntaja (Recommended)**
```clojure
;; deps.edn - better content negotiation library
{:deps {metosin/muuntaja {:mvn/version "0.6.8"}}}

(require '[muuntaja.core :as m]
         '[muuntaja.middleware :as muuntaja])

;; Muuntaja handles JSON, EDN, Transit automatically
(def app
  (-> handler
      (muuntaja/wrap-format m/instance)))

;; Automatically:
;; - Parses request body based on Content-Type
;; - Formats response based on Accept header
;; - Handles JSON, EDN, Transit out of the box

(defn handler [request]
  ;; :body-params contains parsed body
  (let [{:keys [name email]} (:body-params request)]
    {:status 200
     :body {:message "Created"
            :user {:name name :email email}}}))

;; Request with Content-Type: application/json -> parses JSON
;; Request with Accept: application/edn -> returns EDN
```

**Streaming Responses**
```clojure
;; Return InputStream for large files
(defn download-file [request]
  (let [file (io/file "large-file.zip")]
    {:status 200
     :headers {"Content-Type" "application/zip"
               "Content-Length" (str (.length file))
               "Content-Disposition" "attachment; filename=\"large-file.zip\""}
     :body (io/input-stream file)}))

;; Streaming with chunked transfer
(defn stream-events [request]
  (let [out (java.io.PipedOutputStream.)
        in (java.io.PipedInputStream. out)]
    ;; Start background thread to write events
    (future
      (with-open [writer (io/writer out)]
        (dotimes [i 10]
          (.write writer (str "data: Event " i "\n\n"))
          (.flush writer)
          (Thread/sleep 1000))))
    
    {:status 200
     :headers {"Content-Type" "text/event-stream"
               "Cache-Control" "no-cache"}
     :body in}))
```

**Complete Example**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]]
         '[ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.multipart-params :refer [wrap-multipart-params]]
         '[ring.util.response :as response])

(defn api-handler [request]
  (case [(:request-method request) (:uri request)]
    [:get "/users"]
    {:status 200
     :body {:users (get-all-users)}}
    
    [:post "/users"]
    (let [{:keys [name email]} (:body request)]
      {:status 201
       :body (create-user {:name name :email email})})
    
    [:post "/upload"]
    (let [file (get-in request [:params :file])]
      (save-file! file)
      {:status 200
       :body {:filename (:filename file)}})
    
    ;; Default
    {:status 404 :body {:error "Not found"}}))

(def app
  (-> api-handler
      wrap-json-response
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-multipart-params
      wrap-params))
```
How do I serve static files and handle sessions in Ring?

Ring provides middleware for serving static files and managing sessions.

**Serving Static Files**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.resource :refer [wrap-resource]]
         '[ring.middleware.file :refer [wrap-file]]
         '[ring.middleware.content-type :refer [wrap-content-type]]
         '[ring.middleware.not-modified :refer [wrap-not-modified]])

;; Serve from classpath (resources/public/)
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-resource "public")  ; Serves resources/public/*
      wrap-content-type          ; Sets Content-Type header
      wrap-not-modified))        ; 304 responses for caching

;; File structure:
;; resources/
;;   public/
;;     index.html      -> GET /index.html
;;     css/style.css   -> GET /css/style.css
;;     js/app.js       -> GET /js/app.js

;; Serve from filesystem directory
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-file "/var/www/static")  ; Serves from filesystem
      wrap-content-type))
```

**Static File Handler (not middleware)**
```clojure
(require '[ring.util.response :as response])

;; Serve single file
(defn serve-index [_]
  (-> (response/resource-response "public/index.html")
      (response/content-type "text/html")))

;; With Compojure
(defroutes app
  (GET "/" [] (response/resource-response "index.html" {:root "public"}))
  (GET "/app.js" [] (response/resource-response "app.js" {:root "public"}))
  (route/resources "/static" {:root "public"})  ; /static/* -> resources/public/*
  (route/not-found "Not Found"))
```

**Session Middleware**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.session :refer [wrap-session]]
         '[ring.middleware.session.memory :refer [memory-store]]
         '[ring.middleware.session.cookie :refer [cookie-store]])

;; Basic session (in-memory, default)
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-session))

;; Session with options
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-session
        {:store (memory-store)    ; Or cookie-store, redis-store, etc.
         :cookie-name "session"   ; Cookie name
         :cookie-attrs {:max-age 3600         ; 1 hour
                        :http-only true
                        :same-site :strict
                        :secure true}})))     ; HTTPS only
```

**Using Sessions**
```clojure
;; Reading session
(defn handler [request]
  (let [session (:session request)
        user-id (:user-id session)
        visit-count (get session :visits 0)]
    {:status 200
     :body {:user-id user-id
            :visits visit-count}}))

;; Writing session (return :session in response)
(defn login [request]
  (let [{:keys [username password]} (:body request)]
    (if-let [user (authenticate username password)]
      {:status 200
       :session {:user-id (:id user)     ; Set session data
                 :logged-in-at (System/currentTimeMillis)}
       :body {:message "Login successful"}}
      {:status 401
       :body {:error "Invalid credentials"}})))

;; Updating session
(defn increment-visit [request]
  (let [session (:session request)
        visits (inc (get session :visits 0))]
    {:status 200
     :session (assoc session :visits visits)  ; Update session
     :body {:visits visits}}))

;; Clearing session (logout)
(defn logout [_]
  {:status 200
   :session nil  ; Clear all session data
   :body {:message "Logged out"}})
```

**Cookie Store (Encrypted)**
```clojure
;; Cookie store encrypts session data in cookie itself
;; Good for stateless deployments, but limited size (~4KB)

(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-session
        {:store (cookie-store {:key "a-16-byte-key!!"})})))  ; 16 bytes for AES

;; Generate secure key
(defn generate-key []
  (let [key (byte-array 16)]
    (.nextBytes (java.security.SecureRandom.) key)
    key))
```

**Redis Session Store**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {ring/ring-session-redis {:mvn/version "0.1.0"}}}

(require '[ring.middleware.session.redis :refer [redis-store]])

(def redis-conn {:spec {:uri "redis://localhost:6379"}})

(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-session
        {:store (redis-store redis-conn)
         :cookie-attrs {:max-age 86400}})))  ; 24 hours
```

**Flash Messages**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.flash :refer [wrap-flash]])

;; Flash stores one-time messages (shown once, then cleared)
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-flash
      wrap-session))  ; Flash requires session

;; Set flash message
(defn create-user [request]
  {:status 302
   :headers {"Location" "/users"}
   :flash {:type :success :message "User created!"}})  ; One-time message

;; Read flash message
(defn list-users [request]
  (let [flash (:flash request)]  ; Available only once
    {:status 200
     :body {:users (get-users)
            :message (:message flash)}}))
;; Next request won't have flash
```

**Complete Example with Auth**
```clojure
(ns myapp.handler
  (:require [ring.adapter.jetty :as jetty]
            [ring.middleware.session :refer [wrap-session]]
            [ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
            [ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]]
            [ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]]
            [ring.middleware.resource :refer [wrap-resource]]
            [ring.middleware.content-type :refer [wrap-content-type]]
            [ring.util.response :as response]))

(defn require-auth [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (if (get-in request [:session :user-id])
      (handler request)
      {:status 401 :body {:error "Unauthorized"}})))

(defn handler [{:keys [uri request-method session body]}]
  (case [request-method uri]
    [:post "/login"]
    (let [{:keys [username password]} body]
      (if (= [username password] ["admin" "secret"])
        {:status 200
         :session {:user-id 1 :username username}
         :body {:message "Logged in"}}
        {:status 401 :body {:error "Invalid credentials"}}))
    
    [:post "/logout"]
    {:status 200
     :session nil
     :body {:message "Logged out"}}
    
    [:get "/me"]
    (if-let [user-id (:user-id session)]
      {:status 200 :body {:user-id user-id :username (:username session)}}
      {:status 401 :body {:error "Not logged in"}})
    
    [:get "/protected"]
    ((require-auth
       (fn [req]
         {:status 200 :body {:data "Secret stuff"}}))
     {:uri uri :request-method request-method :session session})
    
    ;; Default
    {:status 404 :body {:error "Not found"}}))

(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-json-response
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-params
      (wrap-session {:cookie-attrs {:http-only true :max-age 3600}})
      (wrap-resource "public")
      wrap-content-type))

(defn -main []
  (jetty/run-jetty app {:port 3000 :join? false}))
```
How do I test Ring handlers?

Testing Ring handlers is straightforward since they're just functions taking request maps and returning response maps.

**Basic Handler Testing**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.test :refer :all])

(defn hello-handler [request]
  {:status 200
   :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"}
   :body "Hello, World!"})

(deftest test-hello-handler
  (let [response (hello-handler {:request-method :get :uri "/"})]
    (is (= 200 (:status response)))
    (is (= "Hello, World!" (:body response)))
    (is (= "text/plain" (get-in response [:headers "Content-Type"])))))
```

**Using ring-mock**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {ring/ring-mock {:mvn/version "0.4.0"}}}

(require '[ring.mock.request :as mock])

;; Create mock requests easily
(mock/request :get "/users")
;; => {:server-port 80, :server-name "localhost", :remote-addr "localhost"
;;     :uri "/users", :scheme :http, :request-method :get, ...}

(mock/request :post "/users")
(mock/request :put "/users/1")
(mock/request :delete "/users/1")

;; With query params
(mock/request :get "/search" {:q "clojure" :page "1"})
;; uri: "/search", query-string: "q=clojure&page=1"

;; With headers
(-> (mock/request :get "/api/users")
    (mock/header "Authorization" "Bearer token123")
    (mock/header "Accept" "application/json"))

;; With body
(-> (mock/request :post "/users")
```

**Testing Sessions**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.session :refer [wrap-session]])

(defn login-handler [request]
  (let [{:keys [username]} (:params request)]
    {:status 200
     :session {:user username}
     :body "Logged in"}))

(defn profile-handler [request]
  (if-let [user (get-in request [:session :user])]
    {:status 200 :body (str "Hello, " user)}
    {:status 401 :body "Not logged in"}))

(deftest test-session-flow
  ;; Simulate session by threading session data
  (let [;; Login
        login-response (login-handler (-> (mock/request :post "/login")
                                           (assoc :params {:username "Alice"})))
        session (:session login-response)
        
        ;; Access protected resource with session
        profile-response (profile-handler (-> (mock/request :get "/profile")
                                               (assoc :session session)))]
    
    (is (= 200 (:status login-response)))
    (is (= {:user "Alice"} session))
    (is (= 200 (:status profile-response)))
    (is (= "Hello, Alice" (:body profile-response)))))
```

```clojure
(require '[clj-http.client :as http]

  (let [port (+ 10000 (rand-int 50000))  ; Random port
```

**Testing Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-timing [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [start (System/nanoTime)
          response (handler request)
          elapsed (/ (- (System/nanoTime) start) 1e6)]
      (assoc-in response [:headers "X-Response-Time"] (str elapsed "ms")))))

(deftest test-timing-middleware
  (let [slow-handler (fn [_] 
                       (Thread/sleep 50)
                       {:status 200 :body "OK"})
        app (wrap-timing slow-handler)
        response (app (mock/request :get "/"))]
    (is (= 200 (:status response)))
    (is (contains? (:headers response) "X-Response-Time"))
    (let [time-str (get-in response [:headers "X-Response-Time"])
          time-ms (Double/parseDouble (re-find #"[\d.]+" time-str))]
      (is (>= time-ms 50)))))
```

**Response Assertion Helpers**
```clojure
(defn ok? [response]
  (= 200 (:status response)))

(defn created? [response]
  (= 201 (:status response)))

(defn redirect? [response]
  (#{301 302 303 307 308} (:status response)))

(defn json-response? [response]
  (some-> (get-in response [:headers "Content-Type"])
          (clojure.string/includes? "application/json")))

(defn has-body? [response expected]
  (= expected (:body response)))

;; Usage
(deftest test-with-helpers
  (let [response (app (mock/request :get "/users"))]
    (is (ok? response))
    (is (json-response? response))))
```
